path: Thirty eight interface primitives and twelve patterns. The primitives follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, which is a published standard rather than anyone's work, so each carries a technique credit to its pattern and nothing is built from a capture. The patterns populate a category that was declared and empty, and each is generated geometry seeded through lib/rng.ts rather than a copied output. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, every random number comes from the seed, and every default already looks finished on the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Accordion
components.brief: A set of panels that open and close under their own headers, after the accordion pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices. The headers come from JSON, [{ id, label, disabled }], and the host's direct children are the panels in the same order: set meta.wraps to "panels". For each item the core builds a heading, a real h3, holding a full-width button, and it gives each panel role region, an id, aria-labelledby pointing at its header button, and hidden while closed, restoring all of it on destroy and reapplying it when React replaces a child. Each header button carries aria-expanded and aria-controls naming its panel. With `multiple` off, opening one panel closes the others; with it on, each header toggles on its own. It emits `openChange` with the array of open ids and is controlled through `open` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultOpen`; set meta.controlled to { open: "openChange" }. Keyboard, which the pattern spells out: Enter and Space toggle the focused header, Down and Up move focus between header buttons, Home and End jump to the first and last header, and a disabled header is skipped but stays visible at 45% opacity. Pointer: a click anywhere on the header row toggles it. Look, from the UI grammar: one-pixel hairlines between the header rows, square corners, no shadow, no transitions; the label in the page's font; a mono + on each closed header that becomes − on the open one, drawn in the accent only while its panel is open; a two-pixel accent outline offset two pixels on :focus-visible only. Set meta.stage to "flow", and give meta.demo children of three <section> panels with a short paragraph each. The default frame shows three items with the first open: a ruled stack of headers with one panel of body text. It is wrong if a closed panel still takes space or stays in the accessibility tree, because hidden must carry both; if the hairlines double where two rows meet; or if a header is a bare div instead of a real button in the tab order. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg and accent. meta.interactions: Tab, ArrowDown, Enter, then expect openChange with the second item's id and aria-expanded true on the second header. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 4.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: items (json, default three items, "What Picagram draws" id what, "Where the runtime lives" id runtime, "How the catalog builds" id catalog, none disabled), open (json array of ids or null, default null), defaultOpen (json array, default ["what"]), multiple (default false). The inspector exposes items, defaultOpen, and multiple.
components.events: openChange: the array of open item ids.

components.title: Alert
components.brief: A callout for a status the page must announce, after the alert pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: the host carries role alert, so assistive technology announces its content when the component appears and whenever `title` or `message` changes. It takes no focus, no keyboard, and no pointer behavior, because the pattern is a live region, not a widget. The core builds the layout through a scoped stylesheet: a one-pixel hairline rule above and below the callout, a small mono tag in uppercase tracked text, the title in the page's font, and the message in muted. `tone` chooses how the tag is drawn: "neutral" is a hairline tag box in fg, "muted" sets the tag in muted, "accent" fills the tag's chip with the accent and sets its letters through cssOn so they stay readable on the light ground, and "filled" fills the whole callout with the accent and sets everything in cssOn. Square corners, no shadow, no icon font: where a mark is needed it is a small filled block element, never a text glyph in the accent. Set meta.stage to "flow". The default frame is an accent callout: two hairlines, a filled NOTE tag, a title, and one muted line of message. It is wrong if it carries a tabindex, a role button, or a close control of any kind; if the accent sets running text on the light ground; or if it animates in, because an alert must already be present to be announced. Declare the facets static and text, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 3 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: tag (default "note"), title (default "Build finished"), message (default "All 24 components verified on both grounds."), tone ("neutral", "muted", "accent", or "filled", default "accent"). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Avatar
components.brief: A person or project mark in a square frame: a photo while `src` gives one, the initials of `name` whenever it does not. The frame is a one-pixel hairline with square corners, never a circle. The initials are mono, taken from the first letters of the first two words of `name`, centered in the frame in fg. While the image loads, and forever if it errors or `src` is empty, the initials hold the frame, so the component never shows a broken image. With `dither` on, a loaded image is screened to two tones of the palette through lib/dither.ts on a canvas the core owns, prepared once at load and again when the host resizes; with it off, the image is drawn plain inside the same frame. The host is role img named by `name` through labelHost; an empty name hides it. Set meta.stage to "inline". The default frame is a 48 px hairline square holding two centered mono initials. It is wrong if the frame is round, if a failed image leaves an empty or torn square because the initials were not already there, or if the initials sit off center in their box. Declare the facets static, image, canvas, and dither, and let meta.palette list fg. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 4 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: src (an image URL or data URI, default empty, so it renders with no network), name (default "Ada Lin"), size (24 to 128 px, default 48), dither (default true). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Badge
components.brief: A small status label in the grammar's mono, uppercase and tracked: STABLE, BETA, a version. `variant` chooses the frame: "outline" is a one-pixel hairline box drawn in the tone, "solid" fills the box with the tone and sets the text through cssOn, and "brackets" drops the box and wraps the text in drawn [ ] glyphs. `tone` picks the palette token the frame draws with: fg, muted, or accent, while the text itself stays fg or cssOn and is never set in the accent on the light ground. It is not a kbd: a badge is one continuous label about a status, while a kbd is a run of separate key caps, one per physical key; if the label reads as a keyboard chord it is the wrong component. Square corners, no shadow, small enough to sit beside a heading, and no focus or pointer cursor, because it is not an action. The host is a span: set meta.host to "span" and meta.stage to "inline". The default frame is an accent hairline box around the word STABLE. It is wrong if the box is rounded, if the letters are set in the accent on paper, or if it reads as a button by taking focus or growing on hover. Declare the facets static and text, and let meta.palette list fg and accent. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 2.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: text (default "STABLE"), variant ("outline", "solid", or "brackets", default "outline"), tone ("fg", "muted", or "accent", default "accent"). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Breadcrumb
components.brief: A trail of links back up the hierarchy, after the breadcrumb pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: a navigation landmark named by `label`, holding an ordered list of items from JSON, [{ label, href }], where the last item is the current page, rendered as plain text with aria-current "page" and never as a link. The core builds real <a> elements so keyboard and pointer behavior come from the platform, and it draws a muted mono / separator between items, aria-hidden so assistive technology never reads it. When the trail is longer than `maxItems`, the middle items collapse behind a "…" button the core builds in their place; the button carries aria-expanded, and activating it reveals the hidden items around it rather than dropping them. Links sit in the page's font in fg, hover is a fg tint of about 10% or accent text, and the current page is plain fg. The host keeps role navigation through labelHost with `label`; an empty label hides the whole component. Set meta.stage to "flow". The default frame shows five items with the middle two collapsed: Home / … / UI / Breadcrumb. It is wrong if the current page is a link or lacks aria-current, if the collapsed items are lost instead of revealed by the ellipsis button, or if the separator reaches assistive technology as text. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg and muted. meta.interactions: click the ellipsis button, marked with its own data-pica attribute, then expect aria-expanded true on it. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 3.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: items (json, default Home to #, Catalog to #, Wave 6 to #, UI to #, and Breadcrumb as the current page), maxItems (3 to 8, default 4), label (default "Breadcrumb"). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Calendar
components.brief: A month grid for choosing one date: the calendar half of the date picker dialog in the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, with no input and no popover. The core builds a header row with previous and next month buttons as bare mono glyphs, a month and year heading in a live region so month changes are announced, a row of mono two-letter weekday names in muted with the full names given to assistive technology, and a grid of days, role grid with roving tabindex so exactly one day button is in the tab order. Keyboard, per the pattern: Left and Right move a day, Up and Down move a week, Home and End move to the start and end of the week, PageUp and PageDown move a month, Shift+PageUp and Shift+PageDown move a year, and Enter or Space chooses the focused day. Pointer: click a day to choose it, click the header buttons to change the month. Days outside the month are empty cells, today is underlined in the accent, and the selected day is a filled accent square with its figure set through cssOn. It emits `valueChange` with the chosen date as an ISO string and is controlled through `value` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultValue`; set meta.controlled to { value: "valueChange" }. The visible month starts from `month`, then the value, then today. The host is a group named by `label`. Look, from the UI grammar: mono tabular day figures, a hairline under the weekday header, and a two-pixel accent outline offset two pixels on :focus-visible only. Set meta.stage to "inline", and meta.demo props to { defaultValue: "2026-09-15" } so every capture shows the same month with a chosen day. The default frame is the current month, today underlined, nothing chosen. It is wrong if every day sits in the tab order, if the selection is drawn as accent text instead of a filled cell, or if the month can change only from the header buttons, because PageUp must work from the grid. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. meta.interactions: Tab to the grid's day button, ArrowRight, Enter, then expect valueChange. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 5.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: value (ISO date string or null, default null), defaultValue (ISO date string or empty, default ""), month ("YYYY-MM" or null, default null), weekStartsOn (0 or 1, default 1), label (default "Calendar"). The inspector exposes defaultValue, month, weekStartsOn, and label.
components.events: valueChange: the chosen date as an ISO string.

components.title: Card
components.brief: A hairline container that gives a block of content a header and a footer. Its children are the body, and the core never touches them: set meta.wraps to "content". The core draws a one-pixel fg frame with square corners and no shadow, builds a header row when `kicker` or `title` is set, the kicker in mono uppercase tracked muted above a title in the page's font, and a footer row of links from `actions`, [{ label, href }], separated from the body by a hairline. The first action is a small solid chip filled with the accent and set in cssOn text; the rest are plain links in the page's font, and hover is a fg tint of about 10%. Generous padding, no tint, no rounding. Set meta.stage to "flow", and give meta.demo children of one short paragraph. The default frame holds a kicker, a title, the paragraph, and two footer links. It is wrong if a header or footer row renders when its props are empty and leaves stray rules behind, if the core styles or reorders the children, which belong to the page, or if it draws a shadow or a rounded corner. Declare the facets static, text, and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. meta.interactions: hover on the second footer link. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 3.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: kicker (default "WAVE 6"), title (default "Ship the draft"), actions (json, default Review to # and History to #). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Checkbox
components.brief: A checkbox with a mixed state, after the checkbox pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: role checkbox on the host, tabindex 0, and aria-checked true, false, or mixed. The pattern requires Space to toggle, and the whole host is the target, so a pointer click anywhere on the row toggles too, including the label text. From mixed, Space checks it; after that it alternates checked and unchecked. The core draws a one-pixel hairline square with square corners holding a drawn check glyph in the accent when checked and a drawn horizontal bar in the accent when mixed; the `label` sits beside the box in the page's font and also names the host, and an empty label leaves the box alone, named checkbox. Hover is a fg tint of about 10% inside the box, disabled is 45% opacity, and focus is the two-pixel accent outline offset two pixels on :focus-visible only. It emits `checkedChange` with the new state, "checked", "unchecked", or "mixed", and is controlled through `checked` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultChecked`; set meta.controlled to { checked: "checkedChange" }. Set meta.host to "div" and meta.stage to "inline". The default frame is a checked box beside its label. It is wrong if the mixed state can never be reached, because defaultChecked "mixed" must render the bar; if Space also scrolls the page; or if the marks are an image or an SVG rather than drawn glyphs. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg and accent. meta.interactions: Tab, Space, then expect checkedChange "unchecked" and aria-checked false on the host. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 3.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: checked (true, false, "mixed", or null, default null), defaultChecked (true, false, or "mixed", default true), label (default "Include archived builds"), disabled (default false). The inspector exposes defaultChecked, label, and disabled.
components.events: checkedChange: the new state, "checked", "unchecked", or "mixed".

components.title: Collapsible
components.brief: A single disclosure, after the disclosure pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: a trigger button the core builds, carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls, that shows and hides one block of content. It is not an accordion: an accordion manages which of several sibling panels is open and owns a header for every one, while a collapsible hides one block behind one trigger and is meant to tuck a piece of content away inside a page. The host's direct children are the block: set meta.wraps to "panels", give each child an id the trigger's aria-controls names, set hidden on each while closed, and restore everything on destroy, reapplying when React replaces a child. The trigger is a real button holding a mono ▸ that becomes ▾ while open, drawn in the accent only then, beside the `label` text in the page's font; a hairline rule separates the trigger from the open block. Keyboard is the button's own: Enter and Space toggle. Pointer: click toggles. It emits `openChange` with the new state and is controlled through `open` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultOpen`; set meta.controlled to { open: "openChange" }. Set meta.stage to "flow", and meta.demo to { props: { defaultOpen: true }, children: a short paragraph } so captures show the open block. The default frame is a closed trigger row, ▸ Details. It is wrong if the trigger is not a real button, if the closed block still reaches assistive technology, because hidden must carry it, or if opening slides or fades, because state changes are instant. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg and accent. meta.interactions: Tab, Enter, then expect openChange and the flipped aria-expanded on the trigger. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 3.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: open (boolean or null, default null), defaultOpen (default false), label (default "Details"). The inspector exposes defaultOpen and label.
components.events: openChange: the new open state.

components.title: Combobox
components.brief: An editable text field whose suggestions live in a listbox, after the combobox pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices with list autocomplete, aria-autocomplete "list": the typed text is never rewritten while the user moves through the suggestions, which is what separates it from autocomplete both. The core builds a real input with role combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant, a mono chevron button that stays out of the tab order, and a Popover API listbox of the options from JSON, [{ value, label, disabled }], placed under the field the way select's is, with CSS anchor positioning where supported and getBoundingClientRect otherwise. Typing filters the options by a case-insensitive match on the label and opens the listbox; when nothing matches, a muted row reads `emptyText` and is not an option. Keyboard: Down opens the listbox and activates the first option, Down and Up move the active option, Home and End move the caret, Enter chooses the active option, filling the field with its label and emitting `valueChange` with its value, Escape closes the listbox, Alt+Up closes it, and Tab leaves the field keeping the text. Pointer: click the field or the chevron to open, click an option to choose, hover moves the active option. It is controlled through `value` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultValue`; set meta.controlled to { value: "valueChange" }. Look: the field is a hairline box with square corners, the input text in mono, the options in the page's font, the active one in a fg tint of about 10%, the chosen one with a drawn check in the accent, the chevron in the accent, and focus the two-pixel accent outline offset two pixels on :focus-visible only. Set meta.host to "div" and meta.stage to "inline". The default frame is a closed field with its placeholder. It is wrong if arrowing through the listbox rewrites the field's text, if Escape leaves the listbox open, or if the check and the chevron are not the only accent on screen. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. meta.interactions: Tab, press "d", ArrowDown, Enter, then expect valueChange "dither-field". UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 6 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: options (json, default six entries, Dither Field, Mesh Gradient, Scanlines, Bar Chart, Tabs, Select, with values dither-field, mesh-gradient, scanlines, bar-chart, tabs, select, none disabled), value (string or null, default null), defaultValue (default ""), placeholder (default "Search components"), emptyText (default "No matches"), label (default "Component"), disabled (default false). The inspector exposes options, defaultValue, placeholder, emptyText, label, and disabled.
components.events: valueChange: the chosen option's value.

components.title: Command Palette
components.brief: A modal palette that filters a flat command list, after the combobox pattern and the dialog (modal) pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices together. The host is a real <dialog>: set meta.host to "dialog". The core calls showModal() while open, so focus containment, Escape, and the top layer come from the browser, and it builds inside a real input with role combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant, plus a listbox of the commands from JSON, [{ id, label, hint, keywords }]. Typing filters the list by a case-insensitive match over label and keywords; `emptyText` fills a muted row when nothing matches, and the filter resets on close so a reopened palette shows the full list. The dialog anchors near the top of the viewport, about a fifth of the height down, not centered, and `width` sets its measure. Keyboard: the input is focused on open; Down and Up move the active command, wrapping at the ends; Home and End jump the list; Enter runs the active command, emitting `command` with its id and closing; Escape, and a backdrop click when `dismissOnBackdrop`, emit `openChange` false. Pointer: hover moves the active row, click runs it. It is controlled through `open` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultOpen`; set meta.controlled to { open: "openChange" }. Look: a hairline frame, square corners, no shadow, a mono › prompt glyph in the accent beside the input, commands in the page's font with their hint in muted mono at the right edge, the active row in a fg tint of about 10%, and a backdrop of fg at a low alpha through color-mix. Set meta.demo props to { defaultOpen: true } so captures show the palette open. The default frame is that open palette with its full list below the input. It is wrong if the list keeps a stale filter after closing and reopening, if focus can leave the dialog, or if it sits vertically centered like a modal, because a palette hangs from the top. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. meta.interactions: ArrowDown, Enter, then expect command with the first command's id; a second list presses Escape and expects openChange false. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 6.2 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: commands (json, default five: New component id new-component hint ⌘N keywords create, Open catalog id open-catalog hint ⌘O keywords browse, Toggle theme id toggle-theme hint ⌘T keywords dark light, Copy page URL id copy-url keywords link, Restart dev server id restart hint ⌘R keywords serve), open (boolean or null, default null), defaultOpen (default false), placeholder (default "Type a command"), emptyText (default "No matching commands"), label (default "Command palette"), width (20 to 48 rem, default 30), dismissOnBackdrop (default true). The inspector exposes commands, defaultOpen, placeholder, emptyText, label, width, and dismissOnBackdrop.
components.events: command: the id of the command the user ran; openChange: the new open state.

components.title: Context Menu
components.brief: A menu that opens at the pointer over a region, after the menu and menubar pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices. The host is the region: its children are the content the menu acts on, so set meta.wraps to "content", give the host tabindex 0 so keyboard users can reach it, and draw a one-pixel hairline frame around it with a muted mono `hint` line at its foot, so the target reads as a zone rather than a bare patch. A contextmenu event on the host is cancelled and opens the menu at the pointer; Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key while the host is focused opens it at the host's corner; a long press of about 500 ms opens it on touch. The menu is a Popover API popover the core builds, role menu holding role menuitem rows from JSON, [{ id, label, shortcut, disabled }], named by `label`, placed at the pointer and clamped inside the viewport. Focus lands on the first enabled item. Keyboard, per the pattern: Down and Up cycle, wrapping at the ends; Home and End jump; typeable characters run first-letter typeahead; Enter and Space activate; Escape closes and returns focus to the host; Tab closes without choosing. Pointer: hover activates a row, click chooses it, and a pointer down outside closes. Activation emits `select` with the item's id. Look: the region stays quiet, the menu is a hairline box with square corners and no shadow, items in the page's font, shortcut hints in muted mono at the right edge, the active row in a fg tint of about 10%, disabled at 45% opacity, and focus the two-pixel accent outline offset two pixels on :focus-visible only. Set meta.stage to "flow", and give meta.demo children of one short paragraph the menu belongs to. The default frame is the framed region with its hint. It is wrong if the menu opens somewhere the pointer is not, instead of clamping to the viewport around it; if keyboard users cannot open it at all; or if focus is dropped on close instead of returning to the host. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg and muted. meta.interactions: Tab to focus the host, Shift+F10, ArrowDown, Enter, then expect select with the second item's id. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 5.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: items (json, default Duplicate ⌘D, Rename, Archive ⌘E, Delete ⌫, with kebab-case ids and none disabled), hint (default "Right-click for actions", empty hides it), label (default "Context actions"). The inspector exposes every prop.
components.events: select: the id of the chosen menu item.

components.title: Drawer
components.brief: A modal panel pinned to one edge of the viewport, after the dialog (modal) pattern of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices on a real <dialog>: set meta.host to "dialog". The core calls showModal() while open and close() while closed, so focus containment, Escape, and the top layer come from the browser. `edge` chooses the side: left and right give a full-height panel `size` rem wide, bottom gives a full-width panel `size` rem tall; the panel sits flush with margin 0, its only border a one-pixel hairline on the side facing the page, square corners, no shadow. The core builds a header row holding `title`, linked to the dialog by aria-labelledby, and, when `closable`, a close button with a mono glyph and an accessible name. The host's children are the body: set meta.wraps to "content". Escape, the close button, and a backdrop click when `dismissOnBackdrop` each emit `openChange` with false; it is controlled through `open` (null means uncontrolled) with `defaultOpen`; set meta.controlled to { open: "openChange" }. Look: the panel is filled with bg and ruled in fg, the backdrop is fg at a low alpha through color-mix, and nothing slides or fades, because state changes are instant. Set meta.demo to { props: { defaultOpen: true }, children: a short paragraph } so captures show the panel. The default frame is a right-edge panel with its title and close glyph. It is wrong if the panel floats away from its edge or keeps a dialog's margins, if it animates in, or if the backdrop is an opaque black. Declare the facets static and interactive, and let meta.palette list fg and bg. meta.interactions: press Escape, then expect openChange false. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 4.5 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: open (boolean or null, default null), defaultOpen (default false), edge ("left", "right", or "bottom", default "right"), size (16 to 40 rem, default 22), title (default "Build settings"), closable (default true), dismissOnBackdrop (default true). The inspector exposes defaultOpen, edge, size, title, closable, and dismissOnBackdrop.
components.events: openChange: the new open state.

components.title: Empty State
components.brief: A deliberate empty place, not a component that failed to load: a small drawn mark centered over a title, a line of muted copy, and one action. `mark` picks the figure the core draws in mono box-drawing characters, muted, three to five rows tall: "tray" is an open tray, "magnifier" a lens, "orbit" a small ringed body. The title sits in the page's font, the message in muted under it, and `action` is a { label, href } link rendered in the button grammar: a hairline box with square corners, its label in the page's font, and a two-pixel accent rule beneath the label; hover is a fg tint of about 10%. The composition is centered and measured so it reads as designed, never as a void. Set meta.stage to "flow". The default frame is the tray mark, a title, a muted line, and the one action. It is wrong if it reads as a load failure or an error, which means no spinnerless void, no apology copy, and nothing that looks like a crashed frame; if the mark is an emoji, an image, or an icon font instead of drawn glyphs; or if the action outshouts the title. Declare the facets static and text, and let meta.palette list fg, accent, and muted. UI primitives have 8192 bytes and this one is expected near 3 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: mark ("tray", "magnifier", or "orbit", default "tray"), title (default "Nothing here yet"), message (default "Components you add will show up in this list."), action (json { label, href } or null, default Add a component to #). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Field
